title: A place I know
prompt: Choose the sentence in the present perfect.
options: I have visited Santa Ana twice.
I visited Santa Ana yesterday.
I am visiting Santa Ana now.
answer: I have visited Santa Ana twice.
hint: Look for have + past participle.
explanation: Have visited connects a past experience to the present.

title: A letter from the past
prompt: Complete: I have ___ a letter to a friend. (write)
hint: Write is irregular: write, wrote, ...
explanation: Written is the past participle of write.

title: The match
prompt: Complete: We have ___ volleyball together. (play)
hint: For most regular verbs, add -ed.
explanation: Played is a regular past participle.

title: A new friend
prompt: Choose: She ___ met a new friend this year.
options: have
has
had
hint: She takes the singular helper verb.
explanation: She has met uses has + the irregular participle met.

title: A surprising view
prompt: Complete: I have ___ the ocean for the first time. (see)
hint: See is irregular: see, saw, ...
explanation: Seen is the past participle of see.

title: The question card
prompt: Choose the correct question about life experiences.
options: Have you ever climbed a mountain?
Did you ever climbed a mountain?
Has you ever climb a mountain?
answer: Have you ever climbed a mountain?
hint: Start with Have you ever, then use a participle.
explanation: Ever asks whether an experience has happened at any time.

title: The trip
prompt: Complete: They have ___ to the museum. (go)
hint: Go is irregular: go, went, ...
explanation: Gone is a past participle of go. Here, they have gone to the museum.

title: The unopened door
prompt: Choose: I have ___ tried surfing, but I would like to.
options: never
ever
already
hint: The speaker says it has not happened at any time.
explanation: Never means the experience has not happened.

title: A school memory
prompt: Complete: We have ___ English together this year. (study)
hint: With consonant + y, change y to i and add -ed.
explanation: Studied is the regular past participle of study.

title: Not yet
prompt: Choose the natural sentence.
options: She has not tried sushi yet.
She have not try sushi yet.
She has not tried sushi yesterday.
answer: She has not tried sushi yet.
hint: Use has + participle; yet often goes at the end.
explanation: Yet means the experience has not happened up to now.

title: A memorable meal
prompt: Complete: I have ___ a new dish. (eat)
hint: Eat is irregular: eat, ate, ...
explanation: Eaten is the past participle of eat.

title: A starting point
prompt: Choose: I have known my best friend ___ 2022.
options: since
for
yet
hint: 2022 is a point when the period began.
explanation: Since introduces a starting point; for introduces a length of time.

title: The brave moment
prompt: Complete: I have ___ nervous before a performance. (be)
hint: Be is irregular: be, was/were, ...
explanation: Been is the past participle of be.

title: The finished quest
prompt: Choose the natural sentence.
options: I have already finished my project.
I already have finish my project.
I have already finish my project.
answer: I have already finished my project.
hint: Already can go between have and the participle.
explanation: Have already finished describes a completed action relevant now.

title: A gift
prompt: Complete: We have ___ a gift for our teacher. (make)
hint: Make is irregular: make, made, ...
explanation: Made is the past participle of make.

title: An adventure question
prompt: Choose the correct question.
options: Have you ever ridden a horse?
Have you ever rode a horse?
Has you ever ridden a horse?
answer: Have you ever ridden a horse?
hint: Ride, rode, ridden. The subject you takes have.
explanation: Ridden is the irregular participle used after have.

title: A photograph
prompt: Complete: I have ___ many photos of my family. (take)
hint: Take is irregular: take, took, ...
explanation: Taken is the past participle of take.

title: The road
prompt: Complete: My family has ___ across El Salvador. (travel)
hint: In American English, add -ed with one l.
explanation: Traveled is a regular participle; travelled is also accepted in British English.

title: A long friendship
prompt: Choose: We have been friends ___ three years.
options: for
since
yet
hint: Three years is a length of time.
explanation: For introduces a duration.

title: A kind action
prompt: Complete: I have ___ a classmate with English. (help)
hint: Help is regular: add -ed.
explanation: Helped is a regular past participle.
